dedupe_keys.name: opendss wrapper distribution system co simulator with der controls

description: OpenDSS-wrapper is a Python layer that lets the OpenDSS distribution system simulator take part in co-simulations with distributed energy resource models and controls. It was released in 2021 by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, with Michael Blonsky, Harsha Vardhana Padullaparti, Fei Ding and Santosh Veda as developers, because growing numbers of solar, storage and electric vehicle resources and more communications make it necessary to simulate grids together with other domains. The code builds on OpenDSSDirect.py and the HELICS co-simulation framework. Functions get and set element power, read bus and element voltages and line currents, set switch status, tap positions and other properties, solve in quasi-static time series mode with or without controls, load DSS files and collect circuit results, without the user knowing OpenDSS syntax. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub under the BSD 3-Clause licence at no cost and installs with pip. Caveats: the last commit was in June 2023 with a single tag (v1.5), and the wrapper adds no network data. Simulation uses are time-series distribution power flow with DER controls inside co-simulations. Related records: platform-opendss is the simulator it wraps and platform-helics is the co-simulation framework.
